source: Federal poverty guidelines via data/aca_2026.json (HHS, 2026 plan year); SNAP gross income test 130% FPL (7 CFR 273.9) with broad-based categorical eligibility up to 200% in most states (USDA FNS BBCE list); Medicaid expansion at 138% FPL (ACA §2001) and the non-expansion states as of 2025 (KFF status tracker); the marketplace subsidy schedule from data/aca_2026.json.
confidenceNote: The federal lines are statutory and stable. The two state lists — which states use BBCE above 130% and which have not expanded Medicaid — were recalled, not fetched, and change by legislative session; each row says so and the page says so. Children’s Medicaid and CHIP run far above these lines and vary by state; they are not modelled, on purpose, rather than modelled wrong.
note: Read by engines/cliff.js (D-301). Each program is a multiple of the poverty line for the household size, and a kind: cliff (all of it goes at the line) or slope (help falls as income rises, then stops). The ACA row reads its multiple and schedule from data/aca_2026.json so the two tables cannot disagree.

programs.label: Medicaid, adults
programs.note: Adults under 65 in the states that expanded it. Above 138% of the line it ends; the marketplace takes over with premium help from 100% up.
programs.nonExpansionNote: As of 2025. In these ten states adults without children mostly cannot get Medicaid at any income, and below 100% of the line there is no marketplace help either — the coverage gap.

programs.label: SNAP (food)
programs.note: The federal gross-income test. Most states use broad-based categorical eligibility and lift it, commonly to 200%; modelled at the federal line, and the page says the state may be higher.

programs.label: Marketplace premium help
programs.note: The expected contribution rises with income on the schedule in data/aca_2026.json; at cliffMultiple it stops altogether unless the enhanced rules are extended, which that table also says. The engine reads it from there.
